mvp_scope: OAuth install flow for one platform first (Salla or Zid)
Webhook listener on new order to pull shipping address

WhatsApp message to customer via BSP asking to confirm/complete address before dispatch

regulatory.requirement: Handling customer personal data (addresses, phone numbers) triggers Saudi PDPL obligations (lawful basis, safeguards)
Must be accepted as a Salla/Zid Partner and pass app-store review before distribution
National Address mandate for parcels (SAR 5,000 fine, effective 1 Jan 2026) applies directly to postal/delivery providers, not to this plugin, but sets the compliance deadline driving merchant demand

data_dependencies: No confirmed public API to validate/look up official Saudi National Address records against the authoritative government database (Saudi Post/SPL) - not found in this session
Whether Salla/Zid already validate National Address natively at checkout (would remove the need for this app)
Approval into Salla Partners Portal and/or Zid Partner Dashboard
blockers: If Salla/Zid ship native National Address validation, the plugin's core value disappears
Without a confirmed look-up API, the MVP can likely only do format/completeness checks, not true address verification - a materially weaker product than 'validates addresses'
Marketplace app review/approval timeline is outside the founder's control
results.summary: Technically an EASY-to-MODERATE Salla/Zid partner app (OAuth + order webhook + WhatsApp confirmation) buildable solo within a stretched budget, using free-tier hosting/Supabase plus a ~200 SAR/month WhatsApp BSP plan. The main feasibility risk is not build complexity but data access: no confirmed public API was found to validate addresses against the authoritative Saudi National Address database, so the achievable MVP likely does completeness/format checks rather than true look-up validation - weaker differentiation, and easily replicated by Salla/Zid themselves.

blockers: The candidate's core differentiator - being 'layered on Ejar contract data' via API - is likely HARD, not solo-feasible at launch: REGA appears to gate direct API access behind Commercial Registration plus developer/property-manager registration and a security assessment, a multi-month accreditation process rather than a self-serve API key

results.summary: A manual-entry rent-reminder plus maintenance-log tool (no live Ejar API) is an EASY-to-MODERATE, solo-buildable MVP within a stretched budget. However, the stated differentiator of syncing directly with Ejar contract data is not solo-feasible at launch per search evidence: direct API access appears to require Commercial Registration and REGA developer/property-manager registration plus a security assessment - a multi-month accreditation path, not a quick integration. ZATCA e-invoicing is likely avoidable for residential rent (VAT-exempt), which reduces one complexity source.

stack.frontend: Guided web wizard (Next.js) walking importers through required SABER documents
stack.backend: Node.js/Python for document-checklist logic and shipment/status tracking
stack.ai: Claude to auto-generate/check document completeness against published SASO/SABER requirements
stack.apis: No confirmed public SASO/SABER API for programmatic submission found in this session - workflow likely requires manual portal entry or a partnership with an accredited Certification Body
stack.payments: Moyasar for a flat per-certificate fee or subscription
stack.integrations: Referral/hand-off integration with a SASO-accredited Certification Body (CB), which alone can legally issue the Certificate of Conformity

mvp_scope: Guided document/checklist wizard for the Shipment Certificate of Conformity (SCoC)
Auto-drafted SABER application data from importer inputs
Shipment/status tracking dashboard
Hand-off/referral to a partnered accredited CB for actual certificate issuance
results.build_time_weeks: 5-8 (coding); real launch also depends on securing a CB partnership, a business task outside pure development

regulatory.requirement: Only a SASO-approved, ISO/IEC 17065-accredited Certification Body may legally issue a SABER Certificate of Conformity; a solo founder cannot self-certify shipments
Official SASO fees are fixed (Shipment CoC ≈ SAR 350, Product CoC ≈ SAR 500), separate from accredited-CB professional fees (roughly USD 150-2,500 depending on product complexity)

data_dependencies: No confirmed public SASO/SABER API for automated submission - a workflow may require manual portal data entry (fragile, possible ToS risk if scraped)
Requires a signed partnership/referral agreement with an accredited CB to actually fulfil the certificate, which the founder alone cannot control
blockers: The founder cannot become the certifying body itself (ISO/IEC 17065 accreditation is a lab-grade, multi-year process) - the real product is a thin 'document wizard + referral' layer

Competes against incumbent agencies (Adnovs, Watheeq, PCAS) that already offer the same referral service on top of an already-cheap fixed SAR 350 government fee, leaving thin margin for a pure software layer
No confirmed API means automation value beyond simply filling the SASO portal directly may be shallow
results.summary: Feasible only as a document-preparation/referral wizard sitting in front of an existing accredited Certification Body - a solo founder cannot legally issue SABER certificates, since only ISO/IEC-17065-accredited bodies can do so. The wizard itself is an EASY/MODERATE build, but the business depends on securing a CB partnership and out-competing established agencies on an already-cheap, government-fixed SAR 350 fee, leaving little room for software-layer margin.

The main non-technical risk (outside this validator's remit) is clearly disclaiming the product as tooling rather than legal advice.
